chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was a mukatab (contracted slave), under whom was a free wife, so she bequeathed at the time of her death with a bequest. The people of the inheritance said: 'He does not inherit, and we do not validate her bequest for him because he is a mukatab who has not yet been emancipated, and he does not inherit.' So he (peace be upon him) judged that he would inherit by the calculation of whatever portion of his contract had been emancipated from it.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْمِيرَاث: The heirs or people of inheritance
key_terms.مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنْهُ: That which was emancipated from him (referring to the paid portion of the contract)
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: A slave who has a contract with his master to pay a specific sum in installments in exchange for his freedom

ai.seo_question: How does a mukatab (contracted slave) inherit from his free wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies the legal status of a mukatab in inheritance, establishing that he retains a partial share proportional to his emancipation progress, thereby bridging the gap between slave and free status. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that manumission is a gradual process with immediate legal consequences, ensuring equity for the free spouse while acknowledging the mukatab's ongoing obligations. It highlights the dynamic nature of legal personality in Islamic law, where rights accrue incrementally with the fulfillment of contractual duties.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran and Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, altogether from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a contracted man, under whom was a free wife, so she bequeathed during her death with a bequest. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The people of the inheritance do not inherit, and her bequest is not allowed for him because he is a contracted slave, yet to be emancipated (liberated), but he would not inherit’. So he<sup>asws</sup> judged that he would inherit by the calculation of whatever he had been emancipated (liberated) from it (his contract)’.
